messages:
rahul_acme: Hey team – running into repeated 413s when we try to bulk-ingest embeddings. Sending ~120k vectors in a single upload via Transfer-Encoding: chunked. Curl shows 413 Payload Too Large and no request-id in body. Stack: Node uploader -> our proxy -> redwood embeddings endpoint. Anyone seen this pattern?

maya_support: sorry about that, we can help. Can you paste the curl (sanitized) + exact response headers? Also roughly how big is the payload (MB) and model you're calling?

rahul_acme: here's sanitized curl (headers trimmed):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${KEY}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary @big_batch.json
```

Response: HTTP/1.1 413 Payload Too Large
Date: Tue, 11 Jun 2030 14:12:34 GMT
Server: nginx
Content-Length: 0

big_batch.json is ~72 MB, contains 120,000 objects like {"input":"...","id":"..."}. model: text-embed-1536-small (expected dim 1536). We did earlier get some dimension mismatch on downstream indexer when slices were smaller, but main failure now is 413 from the API gate.

maya_support: thanks. 413 from nginx suggests the proxy/gateway rejected the Content-Length/size. Since you're using chunked upload, some infra components require a Content-Length or have lower limits for chunked bodies. Two immediate mitigations: 1) split into smaller batches (recommended), 2) use our file ingest flow (presigned upload -> create embeddings job) if you need single large payload.

eli_sre: tagging in SRE. @maya_support can you capture the request_id + timestamp? We can check gateway logs for client_max_body_size or buffering errors.

maya_support: rahul, can you re-send the failing request within the next 10m or share the exact timestamp? If you can't, send a provable smaller sample that still fails (like 15k vectors / ~9 MB) so we can reproduce. Also include whether you gzip the request.

rahul_acme: I can't resend the full one right now, but here's a 15k test I just ran at 2030-06-11T14:08:00Z that failed too. I did not gzip. Should I try gzip?

maya_support: yes please try gzip compression (Content-Encoding: gzip) — that will often bring large JSON within gateway limits. Also split to batches where each request payload is <= 8 MB as a conservative heuristic. We'll still investigate server-side limits.

rahul_acme: quick question — what's the recommended batch size in vectors? We don't have fixed token sizes; average doc ~250 chars.

maya_support: heuristics we recommend: aim for <= 5k vectors per request for text-embed-1536-small when average doc ~200–300 chars; or keep payload <= 8 MB. Use concurrency 3–6 to speed throughput. We'll share example code in a sec.

maya_support: example Node pattern (pseudocode):

```
// split arrays into chunks of n
async function sendChunks(vectors, model){
  const CHUNK_LIMIT = 5000; // vectors
  const CONCURRENCY = 4;
  const chunks = chunkArray(vectors, CHUNK_LIMIT);
  await pMap(chunks, async (c) => {
    const body = JSON.stringify({model, input: c});
    const gz = zlib.gzipSync(body);
    await fetch(url, {method: 'POST', headers: {'Content-Type':'application/json', 'Content-Encoding':'gzip', 'Authorization':`Bearer ${KEY}`}, body: gz});
  }, {concurrency: CONCURRENCY});
}
```

maya_support: Python snippet for reference:

```
import gzip, json, requests
CHUNK=5000
for i in range(0, len(vectors), CHUNK):
    payload = json.dumps({'model': model, 'input': vectors[i:i+CHUNK]})
    r = requests.post(url, data=gzip.compress(payload.encode()), headers={'Content-Encoding':'gzip', 'Content-Type':'application/json', 'Authorization': f'Bearer {KEY}'})
    r.raise_for_status()
```

rahul_acme: ok I'll try gzip + chunks of 5k and report back. Two more things: sometimes downstream indexer complained about dimension mismatch (we expected 1536 but index showed 1536 vs 768 mismatch errors). Could that be caused by mixing model names or partial responses?

maya_support: dimension mismatches usually mean either you concatenated embeddings from different model families (e.g., old 768-dim model + new 1536) or the client library truncated/decoded incorrectly. When you chunk, ensure the model arg is consistent across chunks and verify lengths of returned vectors. The embeddings API returns an array with each vector length = model_dim. Quick check script: assert len(vec) == 1536 for first N results.

rahul_acme: one of our microservices uses an older embed model env var. Good catch — we'll standardize that.

ingest-bot: automated note: created support ticket #SUP-4721 and attached sample request at 2030-06-11T14:08:00Z (15k test).

eli_sre: we dug into ingress logs. Observed upstream 413 responses at the gateway for chunked requests without Content-Length > 10MB. Nginx had client_max_body_size set to 20m, but our gateway buffer_limit for chunked was 10m due to streaming proxy config. We're going to increase temporary limit for the customer's tenant and investigate long-term fix (accept larger chunked bodies or recommend presigned file flow).

eli_sre: short-term action: increased chunked buffer limit for tenant acme-data (should prevent immediate 413s for ~72MB but still not ideal). Long-term: adding telemetry to surface chunk sizes causing rejections, and improving docs.

maya_support: rahul — you should be unblocked after the change. Still please use recommended chunking + gzip, since our autoscaling and memory usage is better with smaller requests. Also consider presigned uploads if you have very large one-off migrations.

rahul_acme: confirmed — after gzipping and sending 5k batches with concurrency 4, succeeded. Thanks. We still want a follow-up on the gateway config and official docs for large ingest patterns.

maya_support: will open a docs PR and link it in SUP-4721. also tagging eng-platform to review permanent gateway config.

ops-bot: scheduled follow-up: eng-platform to review 413/streaming behavior — due 2030-06-18.

maya_support: thanks everyone — marking this thread resolved for now. If rahul sees any other failures (like partial responses or dimension inconsistencies), ping here and we'll reopen. :white_check_mark:
